preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines() for x in line.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are within bounds 1 ≤ n, m ≤ 10^5 and 1 ≤ u_i, v_i ≤ n.
Input has exactly m + 1 lines: first line with n and m, followed by m edge lines.
Each of the m edge lines contains exactly two integers.
Graph has at least one node and one edge.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip().split() == sorted(set(int(x) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split()), key=lambda x: (x,))
postconditions.description: Output is a permutation of all nodes from 1 to n, sorted lexicographically smallest.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in stdout.strip().split())
postconditions.description: All output nodes are valid and within the range [1, n].
Output contains exactly n nodes, one for each node in the graph.

postconditions.expression: all(int(stdout.strip().split()[i]) != int(stdout.strip().split()[j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n))

all(any(int(u) == int(x) and int(v) == int(y) or int(u) == int(y) and int(v) == int(x) for x, y in [(stdout.strip().split()[i], stdout.strip().split()[i + 1])] for u, v in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) for i in range(n - 1))
postconditions.description: Every consecutive pair of nodes in the output is connected by an edge in the graph (traversal is valid).
